# Hybrid States DB

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

This PR introduces a Hybrid (In-Mem + LMDB) database to use for fuzzing.

When running long fuzzing sessions the LMDB seems to exhaust available memory (yet to be fully confirmed), while `InMemory` db runs out of the heap space, presumably due to unpruned values.

This design uses in-memory for Blocks and States (with pruning), yet Values are stored in LMDB. The claim is that this should keep both heap and RSS memory in check.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Introduced hybrid state storage backend combining in-memory leaf sets with on-disk persistence for large values via LMDB and LRU caching.

* **Tests**
  * Added test coverage for hybrid state serialization and value persistence.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Walkthrough

This PR introduces `HybridSerializedStates`, a new state storage backend that keeps trie-leaf sets in-memory while persisting large value blobs to an LMDB-backed disk store fronted by an LRU cache. The hybrid backend is integrated into the fuzz node fuzzing workflow: block pruning is now unconditional with a fixed finality depth of 10_000, persistent runs select the hybrid backend via a new `stateBackend` option in `ImporterOptions`, and configuration instantiates `HybridWorkerConfig` to manage both in-memory blocks and hybrid state storage. Documentation updates clarify that historical state queryability is now limited to the pruning window rather than the full session.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~45 minutes

## Possibly related issues

- [FluffyLabs/typeberry#931](https://github.com/FluffyLabs/typeberry/issues/931): The PR implements `HybridSerializedStates` where `markUnused` removes only in-memory leaf sets while leaving disk values intact, directly addressing the reported issue of in-memory values DB never reclaiming blobs on pruning.

## Possibly related PRs

- [FluffyLabs/typeberry#919](https://github.com/FluffyLabs/typeberry/pull/919): Both PRs implement the "dummy finality + state pruning" pathway by wiring `dummyFinalityDepth` into importer/fuzzing and pruning via `states.markUnused(...)`.
- [FluffyLabs/typeberry#930](https://github.com/FluffyLabs/typeberry/pull/930): This PR's unconditional block pruning (via `pruneBlocks` and fixed `dummyFinalityDepth=10_000`) directly ties into the retrieved PR's implementation of `markUnused`-based block/state pruning in the `BlocksDb`/`LmdbBlocks` layers.
- [FluffyLabs/typeberry#773](https://github.com/FluffyLabs/typeberry/pull/773): Both PRs use the same pattern of cloning the previous leaf set and rebuilding the backend `LeafDb` before replacing in-memory leaves in `updateAndSetState` to avoid in-place mutation.
